references.text: Paul mentions that he received forty lashes minus one from the Jews five times. This refers to the practice described in Deuteronomy 25:3, where the limit of forty lashes was set to avoid dishonoring the punished person.
The proverb describes how a rebuke affects a sensible person more deeply than a hundred blows on a fool, touching on the theme of physical punishment and its limitations.
The verse mentions that a rod belongs to the back of the foolish one, linking it to the topic of physical discipline and its appropriate use.
The preceding verses provide context for sentencing, where the judge is to determine the number of lashes based on the severity of the offense.
